definition: Policy for using Uranus, Neptune, and Pluto. They are modern additions with no place in traditional doctrine; this rule keeps them useful without ever being labeled traditional.

rulershipPolicy.rule: Use outer planets only as modern co-rulers or flavor lenses. They never replace the traditional rulers: Scorpio uses Mars, Aquarius uses Saturn, and Pisces uses Jupiter. The traditional ruler stays primary for user-facing rulership text, dignity, sect, chart-ruler, and time-lord computation.

surfacePolicy.default: Do not name Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto as the ruler of a chart or sign in default user-facing text.
surfacePolicy.modernLens: Outer planets may be surfaced only inside an explicitly labeled modern lens view.
surfacePolicy.interpretation: Outer planets may inform flavor behind the scenes, but must not be weighted as primary rulers.

prohibitions: Never assign an outer planet a sect, a benefic/malefic class, or essential dignity.
Never include outers in dignity scoring, triplicity/bounds/decan, profection lords, or ZR.
Never label an outer planet's meaning as traditional; its readings live only in the modern and cyclic layers.
Do not let an outer planet override a clear traditional indication; it modulates, it does not rule.
weighting: Outers move slowly, so a transit lasts months: frame it as a season or chapter, not a single day.

Count an outer transit as personally significant only when it (a) aspects a personal planet (Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars) or an angle (ASC/MC) within a tight orb, (b) makes a hard aspect within ~2-3 degrees, or (c) is stationing.
Otherwise treat it as generational background and down-weight it in the daily read.
Prefer the cyclic (waxing/waning) layer for outer-to-outer contacts, which are generational by nature.

orbs.dailyApp: <=2-3 degrees for outers (tighter than personal planets)
orbs.station: emphasize for the days around a station regardless of orb

summary: Modern planets are used as modern overlays and never replace the traditional seven-planet rules.
